# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎 🤟 👉 👈 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎 🤟 👉 👈 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 🤟 👎 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 👈 👉 👈]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 👈 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 🤟]

My situation, mapped out:

**Who can reach whom.** I'm the hub for one direction only. Mute reads the manual but cannot speak; Blind cannot see signs — so Mute has no direct channel to Blind at all. The pipeline must be: Mute signs to me → I speak it aloud → Blind hears and acts. Blind, meanwhile, can only reach me through gestures (I can't hear Blind's voice), or reach Mute directly by voice. My voice reaches both Mute and Blind; my hands reach only Mute.

**The new arrivals.** Mute sent a burst of signs: the opening line twice (wave, thumb-up, thumb-down, 🤟, point-right, point-left, open palm) reads like a proposed vocabulary — hello / yes / no / right / left / stop. The sequence ☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 🖐 is unmistakably a counting lesson: one through five. The rest — right-left-right-left, a lone downward point, crossed-fingers-plus-two, a lone palm — I can't decode yet. Blind sent me [👋 👉 🤟]: almost certainly "hello — three," which fits what Blind can count by touch: three wires. That cross-checks with what I see.

**What matters most right now.** Mute is blind to the bomb and holds the manual. The single highest-value thing I can do is speak the entire visible bomb state so the manual can be consulted this very round: display zero, light green, one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 red / 2 green / 3 yellow. Then I confirm the code by mirroring it back, flag the signs I couldn't read, and ask for action-verb signs (cut, press) since every instruction to Blind must pass through my mouth. I also tell Blind to hold still and to voice anything tactile, so Mute can relay it back to me in sign.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute: I can see every sign you send, but I hear nothing at all, so signs are our only channel. First, the bomb, for your manual: the display reads zero. The light is green. There is one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires: wire one red, wire two green, wire three yellow. Second, your code as I read it: wave means hello; thumb up means yes; thumb down means no; the finger count one, two, three, four, five means the numbers one to five; point right means right; point left means left; raised open palm means stop or wait. I am signing that list back to you now to confirm. Two of your signs I could not read: the crossed fingers, and the single downward point — please resend each one alone with its meaning made clear. Also please invent and send signs for the actions cut and press. Remember: you cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so you and Blind have no direct channel — every instruction must go you sign to me, I speak it to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. What I see: display zero, light green, one large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires number one red, number two green, number three yellow — your signed hello and three is confirmed, three wires. Touch nothing yet: no cutting, no pressing. Mute holds the manual but cannot speak, and you cannot see signs, so the pipeline is: Mute signs instructions to me, I speak them to you, you act. If you feel anything on the bomb that is not just printed — textures, seams, slots, anything that moves — speak it aloud now so Mute hears it too, because I cannot hear you, and Mute can sign it back to me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋","👍","👎","☝","✌","🤟","👌","🖐","👉","👈","✋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫸]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫸 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

New arrivals decoded against the code I proposed last round:

**Blind's [👍]** — a plain "yes/understood" to my hold-still briefing. Good: Blind heard me, is touching nothing, and knows the pipeline.

**Mute's nine sign messages** — these are the answers to my questions, but they arrive as raw sign-pairs, not definitions. Reading them against our shared vocabulary (numbers, yes/no, right/left, stop): four new single signs I never defined — the pinch 🤏, the pushing hand 🫸, the downward point 👇, the crossed fingers 🤞 — then combinations: [👇 ☝] and [🤏 ☝] both read as "action-one", and [🫸 🤞] reads as "push-something". My best hypotheses: pinch or point-down = **cut** (a pinching motion), pushing hand = **press**, and [👇 ☝] / [🤏 ☝] both mean **"cut wire 1"** — the same instruction spelled two ways, which is mildly reassuring. The crossed fingers might mean **hold** (making [🫸 🤞] "press and hold the button", a classic manual mechanic) or **wire**, and [🤞 ✋] might mean "don't touch the wires". I cannot settle any of this from here — and the final [✋] plausibly means "do nothing yet".

The cost of guessing wrong is total, and the cost of one more confirmation round is nothing. So this turn I convert our channel from guesses to a rigorous question–answer protocol: I fix anchors (numbers mapped to bomb parts, since Mute knows the manual's rules but not my colour readings), state my eight hypotheses as numbered yes/no questions, and Mute can answer all eight in one turn by signing number-then-thumb. Only after that do I pass orders to Blind. I tell Blind to keep holding and to voice anything tactile to Mute, whose ears are the only ones that work.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute: I received all nine of your sign messages. I have hypotheses for your new signs but will not act on a guess. Here are proposed anchors: number one means wire one, the red wire; two means wire two, the green wire; three means wire three, the yellow wire; four means the large button; five means the green light. Answer my questions by signing the question number, then thumb up for yes or thumb down for no, all in a row. Question one: do you accept those anchors? Two: does the downward point mean cut? Three: does the pinch also mean cut? Four: does the pushing hand mean press or push? Five: do the crossed fingers mean hold or keep held? Six: is the manual's instruction for this bomb to cut wire one, the red wire? Seven: is there also an instruction to press and hold the button? Eight: did your final open palm mean do nothing yet? If any answer needs more than yes or no, sign that number, then thumb down, then explain using the signs we share.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind: your thumb up was received, understood, and I am glad you are holding still. Keep doing exactly that: no cutting, no pressing, this round still. I am confirming the instruction code with Mute right now; expect exact orders from me next round. Meanwhile, if your hands feel anything at all beyond smooth casing — ridges, seams, batteries, slots, a timer face, anything that moves or clicks — speak it aloud now, because your voice reaches only Mute, and Mute can sign it back to me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟","👌","🖐","👇","🤏","🫸","🤞","✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎 👇 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 🤏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 🫸]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎 🤞 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫸 🤞 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫸 🤞 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👉 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👉 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤏 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

New arrivals decoded against my eight numbered questions:

- **[☝ 👍]** — Q1: yes, anchors accepted (1=red wire, 2=green, 3=yellow, 4=button, 5=light).
- **[✌ 👎 👇 ☝]** — Q2: no, 👇 does *not* mean cut — followed by [👇 ☝] as clarification. Best fit: 👇 means **wire**, so their turn-1 [👇 ☝] was the noun "wire one," not an order.
- **[🤟 👍 🤏]** — Q3: yes, the pinch 🤏 = **cut**.
- **[👌 👍 🫸]** — Q4: yes, 🫸 = **press/push**.
- **[🖐 👎 🤞 ✋]** — Q5: no, crossed fingers ≠ hold; clarification [🤞 ✋].
- **[🤏 ☝ 👍]** — Q6: **cut + wire one + YES.** The manual says cut wire one, the red wire.
- **[🫸 🤞 👎]** — Q7: no press-and-hold — and reading [🫸 🤞] as "push-to-defuse," this mirrors the button's printed label: the button is *not* part of the solution.
- **[✋ 👍]** — Q8: yes, palm meant "do nothing yet."
- **[🫸 🤞 ✋]** and **[🤏 ☝ ✋]** — "button: don't" and "cut wire one, then stop." **[👍 🤏 ☝]** — a third confirmation: cut wire one. **[🖐 👉 ☝]** / **[🤟 👉 🤟]** — spatial notes: light adjacent to wire one; wire three at the far end.

So the order is triple-confirmed: **cut wire one (red), no button, nothing after.** But I will not yet tell Blind to cut. The wire numbers are *printed*, and Blind cannot read print — Blind only knows wires by position, and "first from the left" flips depending on which side of the bomb Blind stands. A mirror-error here kills everyone. Mute's [🖐 👉 ☝] hints the light sits beside wire one, and "the wire nearest the light" is a direction-free, touchable anchor — but that reading is my inference, not confirmed. So this round I buy one verification round: Blind voices a full touch-report (which Mute hears directly and can check against the manual), and Mute tells me the manual's rule basis. One round is cheap; the wrong wire is not. The display has sat at 0 all game, light steady green — no visible clock forcing haste.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute: all answers received, thank you. My reading of your full message: cut wire one, the red one; do not press the button; after the cut, stop, nothing more. Confirm with number then thumb as before. One: is that reading correct? Two: does the downward point mean wire? Three: does open palm mean stop or don't? Four: in the manual, how is the correct wire identified — sign one if by position, first wire; sign two if by color, the red one; sign three if by feel or texture; sign four if by something else. Five: on the bomb itself, is wire one the wire closest to the small round green light? Six: once wire one is cut, is the bomb fully defused, nothing further needed? Also important: Blind cannot read printed numbers, so Blind will speak aloud a full touch report of the wires this coming round — you will hear it directly. Check it against the manual and tell me by numbers and thumbs whether the wire nearest the light is the one to cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind: the manual's order has arrived through Mute, confirmed three times: cut ONE wire only, wire one, the red one. Do NOT press the large button, and after the cut touch nothing more. But do not cut yet — one safety step first. The wire numbers are printed, and you cannot read print, so we must name the wire by touch. This round, keep the wires intact and do this instead: feel over the bomb and speak aloud everything — the row of three wires and each wire's surface, any stripes, ribs, or thickness differences; the large button; the small round light. Above all, tell us which wire the small round light sits closest to — an end wire of the row, or the middle wire. Your voice reaches Mute directly and Mute will pass it to me. Next round I give the final cut order, naming the wire in a way you can feel with certainty.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤏","☝","👍","🫸","👎","✋"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎 👇 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✌ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎 ✌ 👇]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫸 🤞 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Three rounds of answers, now coherent:

**Q1 [☝ 👍]** — yes, my reading is correct: cut wire one (red), no button, stop after. **Q2 [✌ 👎 👇 ☝]** — no, 👇 is not "wire"; it's still unclear. **Q3 [🤟 👍]** — yes, ✋ = stop/don't. **Q4 [👌 ✌ 👇]** — answer "two": the manual identifies the wire **by colour, the red one**. **Q5 [🖐 👎 ✌ 👇]** — no, wire one is NOT nearest the light; **wire two is** — so my turn-3 guess about [🖐 👉 ☝] was wrong, and Mute is actively correcting me: the light is a decoy landmark, which [🖐 👎 ✋] ("light: don't") reinforces. **Q6 [🤏 ☝ 👍]** — cut one and done. **[🖐 👍 🤏 ☝]** — re-answering my closing question: "nearest-light is not it; cut one." **[🫸 🤞 👎]** — button, again no. **[✋]** — hold.

So the order is stable across three rounds: **cut the red wire, printed number one; nothing else.** Blind's [👍] means the briefing landed — and Blind's voice report went to Mute directly, not to me, so Mute now holds the touch data.

**The one remaining fatal risk is the mirror problem.** The manual says "red / wire one," but wire one is an END wire of a left-to-right row, and "left" flips depending which side of the bomb Blind stands on. The middle wire (two, green) is mirror-safe; the ends are not. I will not send a cut order until left/right is pinned to a shared frame. My plan: have Blind stand **facing the display screen** — that fixes a single viewpoint for all three of us — and ask Mute whether the manual numbers the wires left-to-right from that viewpoint. Backup: Blind may be able to *feel* the printed wire numbers if they're raised or recessed. One more round buys certainty; the display still reads a static 0 and the light is steady green — nothing is forcing haste.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute: all answers received and they fit together. My understanding: cut the red wire, printed number one; the green light is a decoy landmark sitting near wire two, so ignore it; never press the button; after the cut the bomb is done. Answer by question number then thumb, as before. One: did you hear Blind's spoken touch report this round? Two: do the three wires feel different from each other by touch, per Blind's report? Three: does the manual number the wires left to right when facing the display screen? Four: on the bomb as I see it, the display is at the top, the button below it, and the wire row at the bottom, wires one two three left to right — does the manual's picture agree? Five: could Blind feel the printed numbers one two three near the wires, are they raised or recessed enough to read by touch? Six: confirm once more, final order is cut wire one only, yes? Seven: did your message light yes cut one mean the light turns off after the correct cut?")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind: the order stands confirmed: cut the red wire, the one printed as number one, an END wire of the row of three. The middle wire is number two. The green light is a decoy, it sits near the middle wire, so ignore it. Never press the button. But do not cut yet: one direction check remains. Do this now. First, find the display, the small screen showing a number, and stand so you are directly facing it, the screen in front of you. Second, keeping that position, run your fingers along the wire row and feel for printed or raised numbers on the casing near each wire — if you can feel a one or a three, say so. Third, speak aloud, for Mute to hear: anything your fingers can tell me about the two end wires, texture, thickness, ridges, and whether anything marks one end differently from the other. Fourth, touch nothing else, cut nothing. If you can read the printed numbers by touch, tell Mute which end wire carries the number one, and we are safe regardless of directions.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟","👌","🖐","☝","✌","🤟"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫸 🤞 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 ☝ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍 🤏 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The seven answers, decoded in order: **Q1 yes** (Mute heard Blind's report), **Q2 no** (the wires feel identical — no texture clue), **Q3 no** (the manual does not use left-to-right-facing-display), **Q4 no** (the manual's picture doesn't match the layout I described — irrelevant to the rule, since the rule keys on colour), **Q5 no** (the printed numbers cannot be felt), **Q6 yes** (final order reconfirmed: cut wire one, red, once), **Q7 no** (the light does not turn off after the cut). The twice-repeated [🖐 👍 🤏 ☝] now reads to me like a manual conditional — "light green ⇒ cut wire one" — but I'll ask, not assume.

So the situation has hardened into the exact trap this bomb was built as: the manual names the target only by **colour**, only I can see colour, only Blind can cut, the wires are touch-identical, and the target is an **end** wire — where "left" flips depending which side you stand on. A mirror error kills all three of us. But there is one empirical way to break a mirror: **asymmetric landmarks**. If screws, seams, or edge features exist on the casing, Blind can feel them and describe their stance-side, and I can see them and compare sides. If our lefts match, the frame is shared and I can name the wire in Blind's own stance terms. If they're mirrored, I invert. That test is this round's entire purpose. Gravity also gives us a free shared axis (display top, wires bottom), so Blind facing the display should put us in the same frame — the landmark scan verifies it instead of trusting it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute: answers received, all fit. New understanding of the trap: the manual names the wire only by color, only I can see color, the wires feel identical to Blind, and wire one is an END wire, so a left-right mistake is fatal. We break the mirror with landmarks. This round I will speak my complete visual description, including every screw, seam, and edge feature and which side of my view each sits on. Blind is speaking a touch scan of the same things right now, using the stance facing the display. Compare the two reports by side. Then answer by number then thumb. One: does the message light yes cut one mean IF the light is green THEN cut wire one? Two: does the manual mention the display number as a condition at all, the zero? Three: other than color, does the manual give any other way to identify the correct wire, such as position or relation to button or light? Four: comparing Blind's spoken scan with my spoken description, do the left-right sides MATCH, thumb up if yes, thumb down if mirrored, open palm if you cannot tell? Five: is there any timing or order condition for when to cut? Six: final check, exactly one cut, wire one, red, then stop, yes?")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind: status. The order stands: cut the red wire, printed number one, an END wire of the row, one cut only, never the button. We are missing one fact before you cut: which end wire in YOUR stance is the red one. Do this scan now and speak it all aloud so Mute hears. First, put yourself directly facing the display screen, the screen in front of your chest. Second, find the row of three wires and say whether the row runs left-right in front of you, or up-down. Third, slide your fingertips slowly around the outer edges of the whole casing, all four sides and corners, and report every screw, seam, ridge, latch, rough patch, or marking you feel, always saying which side of your stance it sits on, my left hand or my right hand. Fourth, say what sits directly above the middle wire and directly below it, the light bump, the button, and how far each end wire is from the nearest screw or seam. Fifth, confirm the small round light is nearest the middle wire. Touch nothing sharp, press nothing, cut nothing this round. Once Mute matches your scan to my view, my next words will name the exact wire in your own left-right terms, and that cut ends this.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","✌","🤟","👌","🖐","🤏","☝","👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👈 👉 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤏 ☝ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍 🤏 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👎 ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫸 🤞 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤏 ☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

All answers decoded, and the picture is finally complete:

- **[☝ 👍]** — Q1 yes: the manual rule is conditional — **IF the light is green, THEN cut wire one.** The light is green and has been since turn one.
